rows.author: A094
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INSTITUTE COASTAL AND FORESHORE LAND REFORM
rows.abstract: Enables small fishermen and farmer-fisherme n to own small portions of the land along the coast by giving them the right to purchase the same under just and reasonable terms. Designates the Dept. of Agrarian Reform to implement the provisions of this bill.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATURAL RESOURCES since 1997-10-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT CONVERTING THE MUNICIPALITY OF MAASIN INTO A COMPONENT CITY OF THE PROVINCE OF SOUTHERN LEYTE TO BE KNOWN AS THE CITY OF MAASIN
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1997-10-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS TO OBTAIN PUBLIC LIABILITY INSURANCE AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Sesk to substantiate Article 2189 of the Civil Code which states: "Provinces, cities and municipalities shall be liable for damages for death of, or injuries suffered by, any person by reason of the defective condition of roads, streets, bridges, public buildings, and other public works under their control or supervisions." > Seeks, therefore, to institutionaliz e public liability insurance to facilitate the compensation for loss or damage caused by the defective condiction of roads, streets, bridges, public buildings, and other public works.  With this bill, the payment of the compensation by the insurance companies shall be AUTOMATIC, pending the litigation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1997-10-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING INSURANCE COVERAGE TO PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS WHO RENDER ELECTORAL SERVICES DURING REGISTRATION AND ELECTION DAYS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Declares the following --- "SECTION 1. All public schoolteachers who render services during registration and election days shall be provided life, disability and accident insurance benefits." "SECTION 2. The Commission on Election shall promulgate the rules and regulations to implement Section 1 hereof which may provide for individual or group insurance. This benefit shall be granted in addition to any other insurance benefits to which public schoolteachers are now entitled."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 1997-10-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE USE OF THE SAFETY SEAT BELT BY DRIVERS AND FRONT SEAT PASSENGERS OF ALL MOTOR VEHICLES TRAVERSING ALL NATIONAL HIGHWAYS
rows.abstract: "Safety Belt System Act" Provides for the following --- "SECTION 2. All motor vehicles passing through national highways shall be equipped with a safety belt system consisting of integrated lap and shoulder belts which must be used by their front seat occupants." "SECTION 3. No motor vehicle shall be sold or registered and no registered motor vehicle shall be operated unless such vehicle is equipped with safety belts approved by and conforming to standards established by the Land TransportationOffice."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 1997-10-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR THIRD PARTY LIABILITY OF PRIVATE CAR AND OTHER VEHICLE OWNERS AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 377 PARAGRAPH 2 OF THE NEW INSURANCE  CODE
rows.abstract: Rationale: Insurance coverage lessens the heavy burden suffered by vehicles owners for their liabilities in case of death or injury caused to third parties. In addition, it will provide a fast and ready relief to injured third parties or to their relatives. Proposes the following scheme of insurance coverage for third party liability of private car/other vehicle owners: (1) Private Cars (a) Bantam: [Twenty thousand Pesos] THIRTY THOUSAND PESOS: (b) Light: [Twenty Thousand Pesos] THIRTY THOUSANDPESOS; (C) Heavy: [Thirty Thousand Pesos] FORTY THOUSAND PESOS; (2) Other Private Vehicles (a) Tricycle, Motorcycles and Scooters: [Twelve Thousand Pesos] FIFTEEN THOUSAND PESOS; (b) Vehicles with an unladen weight of 2,600 kilos or less: [Twenty Thhousand Pesos] THIRTY THOUSAND PESOS; (c) Vehicle with an unladen weight of between 2,601 kilos and 3,939 kilos: [Thirty Thousand Pesos] FORTY THOUSAND PESOS; (d) Vehicle with an unladen weight over 3,930 kilos: Fifty Thousand Pesos.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 1997-10-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL PUBLIC HEALTH CENTERS TO BE OPEN AT ALL TIMES TO PROVIDE CONTINUOUS HEALTH AND MEDICAL SERVICES TO THE PUBLIC
rows.abstract: Rationale: The problem of health and medical services for the poor in our society is a very serious one.  Free wards of private hospitals and the existing services of public health and medical needs of the people.  This is specially true because after regular office hours, public health centers are closed, and the sick among the poor have nowhere to go for free medical attention. > This Bill seeks to ease up the situation by extending the working hours of public health center beyond regular daytime schedules.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 1997-10-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE USE OF THE CREDIT CARD FOR THE PAYMENT OF OBLIGATIONS TO THE GOVERNMENT, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- "SECTION 1. The use of the credit card for the payment of obligations to the government is hereby authorized, subject to the policies and practices of the particular authorized participating credit card companies; Provided, that, the government shall not bear any burden of discount, rebates or commissions for collection services rendered by the credit card companies." "SECTION 2. Participating credit card companies shall remit payment to the appropriate governmentcollection agencies within forty eight (48) hours upon presentation to them of the charge slips corresponding to the credit card holders' tax payments; Provided, That, should a credit card company fail to remit within the prescribed period, a penaltty of not more than two percent (2%) of the tax involved, per month or any fraction thereof, shall be imposed on the deliquent credit company."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 1997-10-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE PENALTY FOR THE CRIME OF GRAVE COERCIONS AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 286 OF ACT NO. 3815, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: Amends ARt. 286 of the Revised Penal Code to read as follows: "Art. 286. Grave Coercion. The penalty of arresto mayor in ITS MAXIMUM PERIOD  and a fine not exceeding FIVE THOUSAND PESOS (P5,000.00) shall be imposed upon any person who, without authority of law, shall, by means of violence, prevent another from doing something against his will, whether it be right or wrong. > If the coercion be committed for the purpose of compelling another to perform any religious act or to prevent him from doing so, the penalty (next higher in degree) OF PRISON CORRECCIONAL IN ITS MEDIUM PERIOD shall be imposed."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 1997-10-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING ARTICLE THREE HUNDRED FORTY OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AS AMENDED, BY INCLUDING THE UNDUE COMMERCIAL EXPLOITATION OF CHILDREN IN SEXUALLY EXPLICIT ACTIVITIES IN THE DEFINITION OF THE CRIME OF CORRUPTION OF MINORS AND MODIFYING  THE PENALTY THEREOF
rows.abstract: Seeks to amend Art. 340 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended, with the following: "Art. 340. Corruption of Minors - Any person who shall promote or facilitate the prostitution or corruption of persons underage to satisfy the lust of another, INCLUDING THE UNDUE COMMERCIAL USE OF SUCH EPRSONS IN SEXUALLY EXPLICIT ACTIVITIES, shall be punished by prison mayor, and if the culprit is a public officer or employee, including those in government-owne d or controlled corporations, he shall also sufferthe penalty of temporary absolute disqualificatio n. IF THE OFFENDER IS THE PARENT OR THE APPOINTED GUARDIAN OF THE MINOR, THE PENALTY TO BE IMPOSED SHALL BE RECLUSION TEMPORAL IN ITS MINIMUM PERIOD."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 1997-10-02

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A COMPREHENSIVE PERSONAL ACCIDENT INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR STUDENTS IN ALL PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SCHOOLS THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract: Declares the following --- The youth is our country's main resource and hope for a better future. It is in recognition of this role that the promotion of education is enshrined in the 1987 Constitution and given priority by the government. It is lamentable, however, that despite this awesome role, students remain unprotected from the many environmental hazards to which they are exposed daily in the pursuit of an education, such a traffic accidents while commuting to and from school, accidents while attending classes, while at play in the school premised, or while attending school-sponsore d activities and the like. >The effects of an accidents to the student and to the family can be very disastrous. The expenses that the accident entails,as well as, the rehabilitation involved may mean giving up the hope of an education.  At worst, an accidental death deprives the family of ture support from the student. > Considering the foregoing, it is therefore, but fair and jsut that some measur

rows.abstract: Rationale: One of the manifestations of nationhood is a flag and a national anthem uniquely crafted, symbol of its historical evolution and revered by all its citizenry. The national anthem instills in the minds and hearts of everyone the essence ofnationhood. Furthermore, the national anthem encapsules the shared and proud historical past molded by great men and women who labored and toiled for a nation truly their own. > With the passage of time, various arrangements have come up distortingthe original authentic composition of Mr. Julian Felipe. Proposes, therefore, the following amendment to CA 382, As Amended by CA 634: "SEC. 3-A. ANY UTTERANCE IN SPEECH, WRITING OR DRAWING, AND ANY ACT OF OMISSION CASTING DISHONOR, RIDICULE, OR CONTTEMPT UPON THE PHILIPPINE NATIONAL ANTHEM AS WELL AS ITS USE IN PLACES OF ILL-REPUTE OR FOR PURPOSES OF INVOLVING DISRESPECT IS PROHIBITED AND ITS EXECUTION SHALL CONSTITUTE AN OFFENSE. ANY PERSON WHO, EITHER BY HIMSELF OF THROUGH ANOTHER, VIOLATES T
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1997-10-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT REDEFINING THE THIRD LEVEL POSITIONS IN THE CAREER CIVIL SERVICE
rows.abstract: Rationale: Under Presidential Decree No. 807, otherwise known as the Civil Service Decree, positions in the career service with security of tenure include the Undersecretary, Assistance Secretary, Bureau Director, Assistant Bureau Director, REgionalDirector, Assistant Regional Director, as may be identified by the Career Executive Service Board. They are classified as third level positions. > REDEFINES the third level positions in the career civil service as follows: "SECTION 1. All third level positions in the career civil service as defined under Presidential Decree No. 807 shall be appointed by the President, subject to confirmation by the Commission on Appointments: Provided, That no person shall be appointed to such positions unlesshe possesses the following qualifications: (1) Appropriate academic and professional background; (2) career executive service eligibility; (3) Has been occupying another comparable or next-in-rank career position in the government; (4) Has reached th
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 1997-10-06

rows.author: A102
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING PROVISIONAL RELIEF TO CERTAIN VICTIMS OF TYPHOONS, EARTHQUAKES, VOLCANIC ERUPTIONS OR OTHER SIMILAR DISASTERS BY GRANTING SPECIAL DEDUCTIONS FROM INCOME AND REAL PROPERTY TAXES IN THEIR FAVOR
rows.abstract: Provides for the following --- "SECTION 1. Notwithstanding any provision of law to the contrary, any person, natural or juridical, whose immovable property was lost, totally or aprtially destoryed by a typhoon, earthquake, volcanic eruption or similar natural calamities shall be allowed to deduct the total amount of the loss of destruction." Limits, however, the IMMOVABLE PROPERTY referred to in this Act to (1) residential lands and buildings, (2) comemrcial and residential buildings, (3) agricultural lands, and (4) permanently installed machinery.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 1997-10-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT APPROPRIATING THE SUM OF FIVE BILLION PESOS FOR THE AID, RELIEF AND REHABILITATION OF, AND LIVELIHOOD SERVICES AS WELL AS INFRASTRUCTURE SUPPORT FOR, THE VICTIMS OF THE EL NINO EPISODE, CREATING THE EL NINO ASSISTANCE AND DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "El Nino Assistance and Development fund" Declares the following --- "SEC. 2. Declaration of Policy. - It is hereby declared the policy of the State to assist the victims in the communities damaged or destroyed or adversely affected by the El Nino episode and its aftereffects by extending to them aid, relief, rehabilitation and livelihood services to the end that life may return to normalcy at the earliest possible time and the development of the affected areas may not be hampered." Prescribesthe guidelines in the allocation of funds; creates the EL NINO ASSISTANCE AND DEVELOPMENT COMMISSION for this purpose.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 1997-10-06

Establishes, therefore, theSECURITY GUARDS AND AGENCIES SUPERVISORY UNIT (SGASU) within the PNP.

rows.author: B034
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REPEAL PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1818 (P.D.1818 - PROHIBITING COURTS FROM ISSUING RESTRAINING ORDERS OR PRELIMINARY INJUNCTIONS IN CASES INVOLVING INFRASTRUCTURE AND NATURAL RESOURCES PROJECTS OF, AND PUBLIC UTILITIES OPERATED BY, THE GOVERNMENT)
rows.abstract: Rationale: PD 1818, enacted by then Pres. Ferdinand Marcos in 1981, prohibits the courts from issuing restrining orders and injunctions in cases involving development projects of, and public utilities operated by the government. This Act puts an obstacle to the right of the people, the communities, and to question governmental activities which they deem disadvantageous to their health, total development and environment. Essentially, this Act violates the people's right to seek remedies to pursue their right to health and healthy environment as well as their right to freedom of choice. >Seeks, therefore, to REPEAL PD 1818.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 1997-10-06

rows.author: B034
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE FOR THE POPULARIZATION OF LAWS THROUGH TRANSLATION AND POPULAR EDUCATION, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Government should therefore remedy the situation by bringing the law down to the grassroots, so to speak. By translating the laws into languages most understandable to the public, and by presenting the law in the most comprehensive mannerto the people through the use of media and other popular education techniques, it is envisioned that our fellow Filipinos shall be educated on their rights, obligations and possible liabilities under the law. Thus, injustice caused by lack of information can somehow be alleviated. Directs the Sentro ng Wikang Pambansa and the University of the Philippine Law Center to implement a program for the translation of all legislation into Filipino and regional languages for the purpose of making laws uunderstandable to the general public.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 1997-10-06

rows.author: B034
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7832, ENTITLED 'AN ACT PENALIZING THE PILFERAGE OF ELECTRICITY AND THEFT OF ELECTRIC POWER TRANSMISSION LINES/MATERIALS RATIONALIZING SYSTEM LOSSES BY PHASING OUT PILFERAGE LOSSES AS A COMPONENT THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES'
rows.abstract: Rationale: While the rigidity of RA 7832 is understandably due to the proliferation of theft of electricity, yet said law is deemed too oppressive to consumers who might not even be aware of the state of their electric meters and transmission lines/materials .  This bill therefore seeks to temper the oppressive provisions on RA 7832 without being prejudicial to private electric utilities and electric cooperatives. > Proposes amendments to certain provisions of RA 7832, such as on: (1) Inspection and notice of violation; (2) Report on defects in electric meters and materials resulting in lower electricity rate; and (3) Compromise settlement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1997-10-06

rows.author: A007
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 14 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8180, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'DOWNSTREAM OIL INDUSTRY DEREGULATION ACT OF 1996'
rows.abstract: Rationale: Allegations of apparent arbitrary decisions to icnrease the prices by suppliers of petroleum products stem from the fact that there is no agency in government that determines what is "reasonable" regarding oil products. This is an omission in RA 8180 which this bill proposes to cure. > Declares that THE AUTHORITY TO DETERMINE THE REASONABLENESS OF PRICING PETROLEUM PRODUCTS SHALL BE EXERCISED BY THE ENERGY REGULATORY BOARD (ERB).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 1997-10-06

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROCEDURE FOR AMENDMENTS TO THE CONSTITUTION THROUGH PEOPLE'S INITIATIVE , AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE INITIATIVE AND REFERENDUM ACT

rows.author: A041
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXCEPTING FROM PRIVATIZATION CERTAIN TELEGRAPH, TELEX AND DATA COMMUNICATIONS, FACILITIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE 'THE PUBLIC TELECOMMUNICATI ONS POLICY ACT OF THE PHILIPPINES'
rows.abstract: Rationale: The inclusion of the Telecommunicati ons Office in the Privatization Act under Republic Act 7925 was done WITHOUT AMPLE REPRESENTATION from the people of the affected areas. Further, there are NO provisions to COUNTER the effects of the privatization in the affected areas.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS since 1997-10-07

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE REGULATION OF THE ORGANIZATION AND OPERATIONS OF BANKS, QUASI-BANKS, TRUST ENTITIES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: For this purpose, there is a need not merely to review and revise the General Banking Act (Republic Act No. 337, as amended), but to reissue the same as a new law that would govern the regulation of the organization and oepration of banks, quasi-banks and trust entities. "The Revised General Banking Act of 1997" Contains salient features, such as: (1) INCLUSION of universal banks, Islamic banks and cooperative banks in the classification of banks; (2)REDUCTION OF MINIMUM MEMBERSHIP of Filipino citizens in new banks from [70%] to 60% of total voting stock; (3) Monetary Board authority to disqualify, remove or suspend directors or officers of banks, quasi-banks and trust entities; (4) INCREASE in certain allowable equity investmennts; (5) Minimum banking days and hours fixed; (6) DECREASE in loan value of real estate collateral from [70%] to 60% of appraised value.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 1997-10-07

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE OLD-AGE PENSION OF WORLD WAR II VETERANS, AMENDING FOR THIS PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6948, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: The national government has taken a snail's pace in responding to the needs of the now aged, poor and sickly veterans.  In spite of their recorded patriotic services to our country, it is most unfortunate that unlike the veterans of othercountries who are treated with much respect and given full support by their governments, our veterans are struggling for survival, lacking even in their basic needs. > Proposes, therefore, the following --- "SECTION 10. Eligibility - A World War IIveteran shall be paid an old-age pension monthly for life, unless he is actually receiving a similar pension for the same consideration from other government funds or from the United States Government. The amount of the monthly old age pension shallbe according to the veteran's age as shown below:  AGE Monthly Old Age Pension - 65 - 69 years - Five Thousand Pesos (P5,000.00); 70 - 74 years - Ten Thousand Pesos (P10,000.00); 75 - 79 years - Fifteen Thousand Pesos (P15,000.00); 80 - 89 years - Tw
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on VETERANS AFFAIRS since 1997-10-07

rows.title_full: AN ACT MAKING THE CRIME OF MURDER COMMITTED AGAINST BARANGAY OFFICIALS WHO ARE KILLED IN THE LINE OF DUTY PUNISHABLE BY THE MAXIMUM PENALTY OF DEATH
rows.abstract: Rationale: Aside from having lesser compensation for their work, barangay officials lack the protection and security they need in the exercise of their duties. In complying with the demands  of their work, they unavoidably meet the ire of some people. This often results in injury being inflicted on them, or to their death in more serious cases. > With this lowly status of our barangay officials, It is imperative that we provide the security and protection they need in the exercise of their duties. Hence, the attached bill seeks to minimize the occurrence of violence against barangay officials by advocating HARSHER PENALTIES for those who commit murder against our barangay officials.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 1997-10-07

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE MANDATORY APPOINTMENT OF AN ENVIRONMENT AND NATURAL RESOURCES OFFICER IN THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE
rows.abstract: States that the propsoed officer shall ISSUE ENVIRONMENTAL CLEARANCE AND GRANT ACCREDITATION TO TOURISM ESTABLISHMENTS IN THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNIT CONCERNED.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 1997-10-07

rows.author: B043
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE OVERSEAS ENTERTAINMENT INDUSTRY BOARD (OEIB)
rows.abstract: Proposes the cretion of a "single body to effectively and efficiently develop a system to cater to the needs of the entertainment industry." The proposed OEIB shall --- (1) act as clearing house for all training programs and technical assistance formanpower development programs affecting the industry; (2) formulate and implement measures to rationalize the recruitment and placement system and institutionaliz e ethical business standards within the industry in order to ensure the employemnt ofcertified artists and the participation of qualified entities; (3) promote the development of skills and careful selection of performing artists for overseas employment; and (4) institute a system for ensuring the speedy processing of pertinent documments for those who are qualified for deployment.

The mere posession of prohibited drugs, including but not limited to shabu, marijuana, cocaine and the like, shall be prima facie evidence that the possessor is a user of prohibited drugs. rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8180, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "DOWNSTREAM OIL DEREGULATION ACT," BY PRESCRIBING PARITY OF TARIFF DUTY RATES ON IMPORTED CRUDE OIL AND PETROLEUM REFINED PRODUCTS, CLARIFYING AND MODIFYING THE ANTITRUST PROVISIONS OF THE ACT, AND INSTITUTIONALIZ ING THE REMEDIES AGAINST VIOLATIONS OF SAID PROVISIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: "The present bill formalizes the concept of the appropriate actions which may be resorted to under the Rules of Court in conjunction with the oil deregulation law are adequate. But to stress their availability and dynamism, it is a good move to incorporate all the remedies in the law itself. Thus, the present bill formalizes the concept of government intervention and private suits to address the problem of antitrust violations. Specifically, the government may file an action to prevent or restrain any act of cartelization of predatory pricing, and if it has suffered any loss or damage by reason of the antitrusat violation it may recover damages. Likewise, a private person or entity may sue to prevent or restrain any such violatiion which will result in damage to his business or property, and if he has already suffered damage he shall recover treble damages. A class suit may also be allowed.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 1997-10-07

rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING GOVERNMENT HOSPITALS TO UTILIZE ALL INCOME FOR THEIR MAINTENANCE AND OTHER OPERATING EXPENSES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This practice of disallowing government hospitals from spending their income for Maintenance And Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) has the effect of limiting their capability for expansion and improvement and precisely the primary reason why government hospitals fail to deliver quality and efficient delivery of basic health services to the people. Mandates, therefore, the following --- "SECTION 1. Government hospitals are hereby authorized to utilize their income from pharmacy, laboratory, radiology, operating room and nursery for the maintenance and other operating expenses of the hospital. "SECTION 2. Expenditures under this Act shall be subject to existing auditing rules and regulations. In addition, it shall submit quaterly reeport to the DOH their statement of income and expenditures."

The Certificate of Compliance shall be valid for ONE (1) YEAR from date of issue. Penalizes violation of this Act.

rows.abstract: Rationale: This bill seeks to give meaning and substance to Article II, Sec. 26 of the Philippine Constitution which states that: "The State shall guarantee equal access to opportunities for public service, and prohibit political dynasties as may bedefined by law." Contains the following slaient features: (1) No person holding any elective public office shall be immediately succeeded by any person having a political dynasty relationship to such public official as defined in Section 4 (a) of this Act; (2) No person having a political dynasty relationship to an incumbent elective public official seeking reelection shall be allowed to run simultaneously with and for the same office the incumbent public official is holding; (3) Persons runninng for the positions of Punong Barangay and Sangguniang Barangay are not covered by the abovestated prohibitions; (4) Candidates running for any elective public office within a province, except for the positions of Punong Barangay and Sangguniang Bar

rows.abstract: Proposes the following amendment to Section 20, Art. IV of the Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972:  "SEC. 20. Application of Penalties, Confiscation and Forfeiture of the Proceeds or Instruments of the Crime. - The penalties for offenses under Sections 3,4, 7, 8, and 9 of Article II and Sections 14, 14-A, 15 and 16 of Article III of this Act shall be applied if the dangerous drugs involved is in any of the following quantities: (1) [40] 20 grams or more of opium; (2) [40] 20 grams or more of morphine; (3) [200] 15 grams or more of shabu or methylamphetami ne hydrochloride; (4) [40] 20 grams or more of heroin; (5) [750] 350 grams or more of indian hemp or marijuana; (6) [50] 25 grams or more of marijuan resin or marijuan resin oil; (7) [40] 20 grrams or more of cocaine or cocaine hydrochloride; or (8) xxx."

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO DECLARE OCTOBER FIFTEEN OF EVERY YEAR AS NATIONAL RURAL WOMEN'S DAY
rows.abstract: Rationale: Rural women comprise more than one-fourth of the world population, with 500 million of rural women living below the poverty line.  Women produce 60% to 80% of basic foodstuffs in the African Sahara and the Carribean regions. They perform50% of rice cultivation in Asia and 30% of agricultural work in industrialized countries. In Africa, women process 100% of basic household foodstuffs. In spite of their major role in agricultural production and consequently, in the promotion of foodsecurity, rural women are not given due recognition. Mandates, therefore, the following --- "SEC. 2. To ensure meaningful observance of said day as herein declared, all heads of government agencies and instrumentaliti es, including government-owne dand controlled corporation as well as local government units, and employees in the private sector shall encourage and support the holding of activities that will highlight the contributions of rual women to the economy and society."

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING MONETARY AWARDS IN FAVOR OF WORKERS FROM TAXES AND OTHER ASSESSMENTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE ARTICLE 279 OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is generally conceded that workers' monetary claims mature into final and executory judgment only after the lapse of considerable period of time notwithstanding constitutional and statutory provisions mandating their speedy disposition(Section 16, Article III, 1987 Constitution; Article 277(e), Labor Code). Needless to state, these undue delays invariably diminish the value of whatever amounts that shall have been awarded in favor of the workers. Mandates, therefore, the following --- "SECTION 1. NOTWITHSTANDING ANY PROVISION OF GENERAL OR SPECIAL LAW TO THE CONTRARY, ANY MONETARY AWARD IN FAVOR OF WORKERS IN ALL LABOR DISPUTES INCLUDING, BUT NOT LIMITED TO BACKWAGES, SEPARATION PAY, DIFFERENTIAL PAYMENTS, DAMAGES OR THE MONNETARY EQUIVALENT OF WORKERS OTHER PRIVILEGES OR BENEFITS, SHALL BE FREE FROM TAXES AND OTHER ASSESSMENTS. THE EXEMPTION PROVIDED HEREIN MAY BE WITHDRAWN ONLY BY A SPECIAL LAW EXPRESSLY REPEALING THIS PROVISION."

rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING THE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 1997 REPEALING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6425, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is acknowledged that the drug abuse problem in the country is extremely difficult and multi-faceted. > Experience gained in the long years of enforcement of RA No. 6425, otherwise known as the Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972, has providedinsights in improving ways to effectively combat the proliferation and abuse of dangerous drugs among our people especially the youth. "Dangerous Drugs Act of 1997" Contains salient features, such as: (1) Definition of "dangerous drugs" now include athird category, the Dangerous Drugs Preparations in addition to Prohibited Drugs and Regulated Drugs; (2) Penalties and fines have been greatly increased consistently with those imposed by RA 7659, or the Death Penalty Act and the quantity of drugspossessed which will make the act punishable with the death penalty; (3) Dangerous Drugs Board shall be attached to the Department of Justice instead of the Department of Health. rows.abstract: Mandates the proposed Department to serve as the government agency responsible for the development of agricultural and fishery development by providing the policy framework, public investments and support services needed for their modernization. rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING CERTAIN ACTS OR TRANSACTIONS IN GOVERNMENT OFFICES AS "FIXING" AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Rationale: Fixing has long been recognized as a source of graft and corruption and has been accepted as a common occurence in the bureaucracy. While government offices have set-up procedural rules to ensure expeditious actions, these rules have beentaken lightly by fixers who wrok in cahoots with certain public officials and employees in consideration of grease money and other forms of personal gain. "Anti-Fixing Law of 1997" Mandates the PUBLIC POSTING OF PROCEDURES --- "All government offices, agencies, including government-owne d and/or controlled corporations, where the public transacts business on a regular and routinary basis, shall post signs in prominent places within their premises with the following information written in Pilipiino or in the local dialect." Provides other areas of concern, such as (1) Setting up of a Public Service Unit in each office;  (2) staggard work hours; issuance of appointment ship; and wearing of name plates. Penalizes violation of this Act.
rows.status: Bill reported out 1997-10-10 (#01134)

rows.author: A001
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE SUBSTITUTION OF CANDIDATES BY ANOTHER IN CASE OF DISQUALIFICATIO N AND WITHDRAWAL, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION SEVENTY-SEVEN OF BATAS PAMBANSA BILANG EIGHTY-EIGHT HUNDRED ANDONE, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: Under Section 77 of Batas Pambansa Blg. 881, substitution of candidates in case of unexpected or fortuitous event is permitted so as not to deprive  a registered or accredited political party the right to field its own candidate. > Politicians however have often subverted the legislative intent behind this remedy by engaging intoo much horsetrading, bargaining and secret deals, sometimes with violent consequences. Hence, it is not surprising that most of these politicians file theircertificates of candidacy at the last minute. Contains these salient features: (1) Substitution of candidates shall only be allowed inc ase of death; and (2) In the case of independent candidates, the substitute shall only come from a list of three ((3) persons submitted by the independent candidate concerned at the time he filed his certificate of candidacy according to their ranking in said list.
rows.status: Bill reported out 1997-10-10 (#01135)
